question_text:
Paige invests €$500$ in an account that pays $7.2\%$ p.a. compounded monthly.
The amount of money in Paige's account at the end of each month follows a geometric sequence with common ratio $r$.

subparts.solution:
$$\text{If the interest rate per annum is } 7.2\%, \text{ then the interest rate per month } i = \frac{7.2\%}{12} = 0.6\% = 0.006.$$
$$r = 1 + i$$
$$= 1 + 0.006$$
$$= 1.006$$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Monthly interest rate is the annual nominal interest rate divided by 12. The growth multiplier is $r = 1 + i$.
step_by_step: Add 1 to get the monthly multiplier: $r = 1.006$.

subparts.stem: Find the value of the account after $3$ years.

mark_breakdown.desc: Computing final amount to 2 decimal places: €$620.15$

subparts.solution:
$$\text{The interest is calculated monthly, so } n = 3 \times 12 = 36 \text{ time periods.}$$
$$u_{36} = u_0 \times r^{36}$$
$$= 500 \times (1.006)^{36}$$
$$\approx 620.15$$
$$\text{The value of the account after 3 years is } \text{€}620.15.$$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Compound amount after $n$ periods is $FV = PV(1 + i)^n$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Using $n = 3$ years instead of the number of monthly periods $n = 36$.

subparts.stem: Given that inflation averages $2\%$ p.a. over the $3$ years, find the real value of the investment after $3$ years.

mark_breakdown.desc: Setting up equation relating real value and inflation: $\text{real value} \times (1.02)^3 = 620.15$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Real value adjusted for inflation over $t$ years is $\text{Real Value} = \frac{\text{Nominal Value}}{(1 + \text{inflation rate})^t}$.
step_by_step: Conclude that the real value after inflation is €584.38.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Multiplying the final value by $(1 - 0.02)^3$ instead of dividing by $(1.02)^3$.
